purpose: DARK PHASE's visible 'red eye glow' asset — extracted directly from the previously-attached DARK PHASE GABRIEL render, not a new Canvas-drawn design.
source: assets/boss/source/dark_phase_source.png (unmodified, byte-identical to the original attachment — md5 0bfba129c9d4b54c9f701cffb5e20e47, unchanged from when it was first saved)
processing: Non-generative extraction only -- no AI redraw/regeneration, no new glow shape/count/position invented. Reuses the EXACT SAME redness classification already verified when building assets/boss/dark_phase.png (see dark_phase_build_meta.json): redness = R - max(G,B); pixels with redness > 15 (the same threshold, not a new judgment call) are the glow. This batch differs from that earlier pass only in what happens to the REMAINING pixels: instead of recoloring the black-body pixels to an opaque black silhouette, EVERY non-glow pixel (both the original white background AND the black body/wings) is set fully transparent (alpha=0). The glow pixels themselves keep their exact original RGB and go to full opacity, completely unmodified in shape, count, or position.
result: 7303 glow pixels, bounding box x:[554,648] y:[289,405] in the original 1152x1728 source canvas -- a tight cluster of the mask's glowing red eye + vent-slit shapes, matching the visor pattern visible in the original attached image exactly (nothing added, nothing moved).
crop: Cropped to that bounding box plus a 20px margin on every side (crop box [534,269]-[669,426] in source coordinates) and saved at that crop's native resolution -- no resize/stretch. Final file: assets/boss/dark_phase_eyes.png, 135x157px.
white_halo_check: Since every non-glow pixel (including all originally-white-background and originally-black-body pixels) is forced to alpha=0 rather than being partially blended, there is no partial-alpha edge zone left to carry any white/gray fringe -- confirmed by compositing the crop over solid black, dark-navy, and mid-gray test backgrounds: the glow reads as a clean, isolated red light source with no halo, no ring, no background bleed. (0.67% of the glow's own pixels are a near-white/pink hot-core highlight at R=255 with G/B around 180-210 -- an intentional bright-center feature of the original glow itself, not a background artifact, and left untouched per the 'do not alter the glow's own shape' instruction.)
in_game_placement: The ANCHOR point (single source of truth for both drawing and the FLASH hit-test) is computed via the same scale GABRIEL's full body would use if drawn (DARKPHASE_SCALE, matched to the front CINEMATIC image's body-fill fraction, same method as CINEMATIC_BACK_SCALE): the crop's own bbox-center in source coordinates is mapped through that scale and re-centered on boss.x/boss.y -- see DARKPHASE_HEAD_CANVAS_X/Y and getDarkPhaseHeadScreenPos() in game.js. It moves in perfect lockstep with boss.x/boss.y as GABRIEL's STALK/CLOSE-IN/PAUSE/LUNGE/ARC-CLAW/DISENGAGE AI moves it, and the SAME anchor drives the FLASH head-aim hit-test, so the visible glow and the hit-test can never drift apart.
display_size: The body-accurate DARKPHASE_SCALE projection alone would draw this crop at only ~10-12px tall on a phone screen (anatomically correct for a human head against a ~174px-tall full body, but too small to read as 'glowing eyes in the dark' during actual play). A deliberate, disclosed judgment call: the image is drawn at a fixed DARKPHASE_EYES_DISPLAY_H=46px (width derived from the crop's own aspect ratio, so the shape is never stretched/distorted), still centered on the exact same anchor point used for the hit-test -- a uniform resize is explicitly permitted processing, and the crop's internal pattern/proportions are otherwise completely unchanged from the extracted source.
pause_brightness_boost: During the AI's own brief PAUSE sub-state (the telegraph beat right before LUNGE), the eyes image is drawn through a temporary canvas brightness filter (ctx.filter = 'brightness(...)') -- a pixel-value rescale of the SAME image, not a new shape or an added light source, per the 'alpha/brightness only, no new eyes' instruction.
